name: goja-runtime-string-provenance-tracking
instr:
goja cannot trace final UTF-16 string ranges back to literals, host values, JSON tokens, or transformations. Add opt-in provenance that stays precise across JavaScript operations, Go wrappers, and repeated Program executions without changing ordinary string behavior.

Reported ranges use ECMAScript UTF-16 coordinates, with supplementary characters occupying two positions and unpaired surrogates remaining individually attributable. Provenance inspection leaves existing string representation and deferred classification behavior unchanged. Composition and transformation produce ordered, output-relative contributions. Copied units retain their origins; new text and JSON syntax get generated origins. Regexp matches, captures, replacements, splits, and JSON decoding use actual UTF-16 boundaries, including escapes and unmatched captures. Keep literal, host, JSON, reflected-field, map-entry, and slice-element origins distinct even when contents match. Snapshots are immutable, concurrently inspectable, independent of runtime lifetime, and reject invalid slices deterministically without affecting later results. Enabling provenance must not change string contents, representation behavior, equality, iteration, indexed properties, exceptions, or Go exports. Reusing a runtime-independent Program preserves source names and coordinates but allocates fresh runtime-local origin identities on each execution. `StringProvenance.Ranges` and `StringProvenance.Origins` are value-receiver, no-argumen
